leftEvidence.role: Law, righteousness, and the inner life
leftEvidence.title: Murder language reaches anger, speech, and reconciliation

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus recalls the murder command and extends danger of judgment to anger and contemptuous speech.
points.right: James contrasts human anger with God’s righteousness and calls hearers to receive the implanted word.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: A worshiper must seek reconciliation, and an adversary must be addressed before judgment closes the opportunity.
points.right: Hearing without doing is self-deception; continued doing, disciplined speech, care, and integrity characterize undefiled practice.

payload.posture: Matthew traces anger toward judgment and reconciliation; James says human anger does not produce God’s righteousness.

rightEvidence.title: Anger, hearing, doing, and the law of freedom

payload.tension: The sources share concern about anger but address different actions and community settings.
payload.title: Anger and righteousness
